patients.summary: Healthy elementary school teacher who joined in 2023. Hyperemesis gravidarum with two ED visits in her first pregnancy (2025), last seen at 30 weeks; a term delivery, then a second pregnancy with a right ureteral stone that passed (2026), known to the practice only through records and messages.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
25 y/o F, new to the practice, transferring care from her prior primary care office. Teaches elementary school. No complaints today, just wants a doctor she can reach.

PMH: none. No chronic illness, no hospitalizations.
PSH: tonsils out as a child (around age 8); wisdom teeth pulled at 20.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
FHx: mother was hospitalized for severe vomiting in pregnancy (hyperemesis). A maternal uncle keeps getting kidney stones, calcium oxalate per family. Paternal grandmother has type 2 diabetes.
SHx: married. Never smoked. Does not drink at all. Elementary school teacher.
GYN: regular cycles. Last Pap at prior office in 2022, normal per patient; requested records.

ROS negative across systems.

Exam: well appearing, pleasant. HEENT normal, tonsils surgically absent. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin clear. Neuro grossly intact. Mood bright.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P: healthy adult, establishing care.
- Screening: CBC, lipids today (never had a lipid panel), one-time HIV and hep C screens; she agrees.
- Pap: due 2025, will confirm from records.
- Vaccines: will review prior records for Tdap and COVID; flu shot in October at a nurse visit.
- Return next year for a physical, or message any time.

documents.body: Hi Leah, everything from Tuesday came back fine. Blood counts normal, cholesterol in a healthy range, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do. Nice to meet you.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
26F here for yearly physical, came straight from her classroom. Feels well. No new problems this year.

They are hoping to try for a pregnancy over the next few months and she wanted to talk about what to do beforehand. Cycles regular. No meds. Never smoked, no alcohol.

We talked through preconception basics: start a prenatal vitamin with iron now so the folate is on board ahead of conception; she is immune to measles and chickenpox by vaccine history (2 doses each documented); flu and COVID shots are reasonable and safe either way. I mentioned her mother's hyperemesis history: worth telling her OB early, since it can run in families. She laughed and said her mom brings it up every holiday.

Exam: normal. Wt 61.6. Heart and lungs normal, abdomen benign, thyroid not enlarged.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P
1. Preventive care: up to date. Labs from last year were normal, nothing needed today. Pap due next year (2022 normal); OB can do it if she is pregnant by then.
2. Preconception: prenatal vitamin with iron, 1 daily, sent to pharmacy. Message me with a positive test and we'll get her to OB.
3. Flu and 2024-25 COVID given today.
RTC 1 year.

orders.reason: new pregnancy, 5 weeks; mother with hyperemesis gravidarum

documents.title: Positive test!
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning! I took a home test this morning and it was positive. First day of my last period was February 3. What do I do next? I've been taking the prenatal vitamin since September.

documents.title: RE: Positive test!
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Leah, this is wonderful news. By your dates you're about 5 weeks, due around November 10. Keep the prenatal vitamin going. I've placed a referral to obstetrics; they usually like to see you around 7 to 8 weeks and will do the first ultrasound. Please tell them about your mom's hyperemesis. If you start vomiting to the point you can't keep fluids down, call us or them the same day, don't wait it out.

New OB Visit, 3/24/2025
Re: Leah Fleming, G1P0

Meds: prenatal vitamin with iron daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Family history noted: mother with hyperemesis requiring admission. We discussed early warning signs and when to call.

documents.title: Emergency Department Provider Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
COMMUNITY EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival 13:40.

CC: vomiting x 10 days, no fluids kept down x 2 days.

HPI: 26 y/o G1 at 9w2d by LMP, viable single IUP on ultrasound at 7 weeks with her OB. Over the last ten days she has been throwing up after almost every meal, and since Monday cannot hold down even water. Tired, lightheaded when she stands up. Denies fever, belly pain, diarrhea. Urine pregnancy test was positive at 5 weeks.

PMH: none. PSH: tonsillectomy (child), wisdom teeth (age 20).
Meds: prenatal vitamin with iron daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother had hyperemesis, was admitted for it. Maternal uncle with recurrent calcium oxalate stones. Paternal grandmother DM2.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol (pregnant), teaches elementary school.

Vitals on arrival: HR 110, BP 90/60.
Exam: thin, tired-appearing young woman. Mucous membranes dry. Orthostatic: mild drop in pressure on standing. Weight 57.7 kg, down 3.5 kg from her first prenatal visit (61.2). Abdomen soft, nontender. Fetal heart tones present on handheld check.

UA: ketones moderate.

ED course: 2 L IV lactated Ringer's, ondansetron 4 mg IV, thiamine 100 mg IV. Nausea eased; tolerated crackers and ginger ale x 2 without emesis. Repeat HR 88.

Impression: hyperemesis gravidarum with dehydration and ketonuria.
Disposition: home. Rx ondansetron 4 mg ODT q8h prn; doxylamine/pyridoxine 10/10 mg DR, 1 at bedtime. Small frequent sips. Call OB tomorrow. Return for inability to keep fluids, fainting, abdominal pain, bleeding.

documents.title: ED visit notification
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: ED record from 4/9/2025 received by fax (hyperemesis, discharged home). Filed and routed to PCP. Called pt: she is booked Friday 4/11 for a follow-up.

documents.title: Office Visit: ED follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Seen in the ED Wednesday at 9 weeks for hyperemesis, got 2 L and went home on ondansetron as needed plus doxylamine-pyridoxine at night. Since then she has thrown up twice a day instead of after every meal and is keeping down water, broth, toast. Using ondansetron about twice a day. A little constipated. Took two sick days. OB office called her yesterday and moved up her next visit.

O: Looks tired but better. Mucous membranes moist. Wt 58.0 (ED 57.7). Abdomen soft, nontender.

A/P: Hyperemesis gravidarum, improving on the ED regimen. Dehydration improving.
- Continue ondansetron prn and doxylamine-pyridoxine at bedtime. OB to adjust as needed; I'd defer dosing changes to them.
- Fluids in small amounts all day; water bottle on her desk at school.
- Lower threshold for return: if she can't keep liquids for 12 hours, message me or go back.
- Recheck in a few weeks or sooner.

documents.title: Emergency Department Provider Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
COMMUNITY EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT

Chief complaint: nausea and vomiting, can't keep anything down x 2 days.

26 y/o G1 at 12w6d, seen here 4/9 for hyperemesis. Had been doing much better for a couple of weeks on ondansetron and doxylamine/pyridoxine. Since Friday she is vomiting every two to three hours and has kept nothing down, not even water. No diarrhea, no abdominal pain, no fever, no travel. Under the care of an outside obstetric group.

Meds: prenatal vitamin with iron; ondansetron 4 mg ODT prn; doxylamine/pyridoxine 10/10 qhs. NKDA.
Family: mother with hyperemesis needing admission; maternal uncle with calcium oxalate stones; paternal grandmother DM2.
Never smoker, no alcohol, teacher.

HR 104, BP 102/64.
Exam: fatigued, mildly dry. Mucous membranes dry. Orthostatic BP changes present. Abdomen soft, no tenderness, no rebound.

We sent electrolytes and a venous gas to sort out her volume and acid-base status.
Na 134, K 3.1, Cl 92, HCO3 32, BUN 19, Cr 0.6, glucose 76. Venous pH 7.48, pCO2 46. Urine ketones large.
Picture is a hypokalemic, hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis from ongoing vomiting with volume depletion.

Course: NS 1 L then D5 NS with 20 mEq KCl/L x 1 L. Metoclopramide 10 mg IV, thiamine 100 mg IV. By afternoon sipping juice and broth without vomiting. Discussed with on-call OB, who agreed with discharge and will see her this week.

Dx: hyperemesis gravidarum with metabolic disturbance (hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis), dehydration.
Dispo: home. KCl 20 mEq ER daily x 5 days. Continue current antiemetics. Repeat BMP with PCP in 2 to 3 days. Return precautions reviewed.

documents.title: ED record 5/4
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second ED visit for hyperemesis received (5/4). K 3.1, sent home on 5 days of potassium. ED asks for a BMP in 2-3 days. Called pt, sounds tired but kept breakfast down. Booked Wed 5/7 with PCP, BMP order in.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit: second ED follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back after a second ED visit Sunday at 12w6d: vomiting q2-3h, K 3.1 with a contraction alkalosis, fluids with potassium, home on 5 days of KCl.

Since then: no vomiting for two days. Eating small amounts, mostly bland, and drinking. Taking the KCl, on day 3 of 5. OB saw her Monday; they're keeping the same antiemetics for now.

Exam: Wt 56.8. Mucous membranes moist. No orthostatic symptoms on standing today. Abdomen soft.

A/P
1. Hyperemesis gravidarum, second ED visit, now tolerating intake. Dehydration has resolved clinically.
2. Hypokalemia/alkalosis from vomiting: BMP today, finish the KCl.
3. She asked if this will last the whole pregnancy. Told her many people turn a corner in the second trimester, but not all; OB is steering.
Will message results.

documents.title: Potassium back to normal
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Leah, your potassium is back up to 3.8 and the other salts and your kidney number are normal. Finish the last two days of potassium and you're done with it. Hope today is a good food day.

documents.title: Obstetrics 20-week visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OBSTETRIC GROUP
Progress note, 6/24/2025, 20w1d

Hyperemesis much improved. Some nausea at the end of the day; no vomiting for about two weeks. Not using ondansetron. Eating three meals.
Plan: stop ondansetron and doxylamine/pyridoxine; she can call if symptoms return. Continue prenatal vitamin.
BP normal. Fundal height appropriate. Fetal heart tones normal.
Anatomy ultrasound today normal.
RTC 4 weeks. Glucose screen at 24-28 weeks.

--- Received and filed, med list updated.

27F G1 at 30w4d, here to check in and get her pregnancy vaccines; OB is fine with us giving them.

Feeling well. No vomiting since June. Appetite good. Back in the classroom this week, tired by afternoon but managing. Seeing OB every 2 weeks soon. Still on the prenatal vitamin, off the nausea meds.

Exam: Wt 64.5 (61.6 pre-pregnancy). BP normal. Gravid abdomen. No edema.

2. Pregnancy, 30 weeks, uncomplicated since. OB managing.
3. Tdap and flu given today.
I'll see her after the baby comes; postpartum care with OB first. Message me any time.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER, BIRTHING UNIT
Admit 11/7/2025 21:30. Discharge 11/9/2025.

27 y/o G1P0 at 39w4d admitted in spontaneous active labor. Pregnancy notable for hyperemesis gravidarum in the first trimester with two ED visits, resolved by 20 weeks. Otherwise uncomplicated prenatal course. NKDA.

Delivery 11/8/2025 04:52 at 39w5d: spontaneous vaginal delivery of a liveborn infant, vigorous at birth, routine newborn care. Placenta delivered intact. Estimated blood loss within normal range. No laceration requiring repair.

Postpartum course uncomplicated. Ambulating, voiding, tolerating diet, pain controlled. Vital signs normal throughout.

Discharge diagnosis: term spontaneous vaginal delivery.
Meds at discharge: prenatal vitamin with iron daily.
Follow-up: obstetrics postpartum visit in about 6 weeks.

documents.title: Delivery discharge summary received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Discharge summary from birthing unit, 11/7-11/9/2025, received via fax and scanned. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Congratulations
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Leah, I just saw the hospital summary come through. Congratulations to you all. Rest up, and reach out if you need anything. Your OB will see you in about six weeks; after that, let's get you in here sometime this winter.

documents.title: Obstetrics postpartum visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OBSTETRIC GROUP
Postpartum visit, 12/17/2025

Six weeks after a spontaneous vaginal delivery at 39w5d. Recovering well. Bleeding stopped. Mood good, sleeping in stretches. Pelvic exam normal, uterus involuted. BP normal.
Continue prenatal vitamin while recovering. Return to us as needed; routine primary care with her PCP.

--- Filed.

documents.title: News
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted to let you know I'm pregnant again! Earlier than we planned, but we're happy. LMP was February 2. I already saw my OB group and the early ultrasound looked good. So far no vomiting at all, fingers crossed. Still taking the prenatal vitamin. I know I owe you a visit, the baby has made it hard to get anywhere. Anything I should be doing?

documents.title: RE: News
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations, Leah. That puts you around 5 weeks, due early November. Keep the prenatal vitamin. Since you had hyperemesis last time, don't be a hero if it starts again: tell your OB early, the medicines work better before you're dehydrated. Come see me when life allows; no rush on our end.

reports.text: Indication: right flank pain, pregnant, 9 weeks. Right kidney 11.2 cm, normal cortical thickness and echogenicity. Mild right hydronephrosis. A 5 mm echogenic shadowing stone at the right ureterovesical junction with twinkle artifact. Right ureteral jet not seen during the exam; left jet present. Left kidney 11.0 cm, normal, no hydronephrosis or stone. Bladder normal. Limited view of the uterus shows an intrauterine pregnancy with fetal cardiac activity.
reports.conclusion: 5 mm right ureterovesical junction stone with mild right hydronephrosis. Normal left kidney. Intrauterine pregnancy with cardiac activity.

documents.title: Emergency Department Provider Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
COMMUNITY EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT

CC: right flank pain.

27 y/o G2P1 at 9w6d (LMP 2/2/26). Sudden severe right flank pain starting around 8 PM, now 6 hours, moving down into the right groin. Nauseated, has not vomited. No fever, no burning, no frequency. Prenatal course so far has been uncomplicated, no hyperemesis this time. Last here a year ago with hyperemesis in her first pregnancy.

PMH: hyperemesis gravidarum (prior pregnancy). PSH: tonsillectomy, wisdom teeth. Meds: prenatal vitamin. NKDA.
Family: maternal uncle with recurrent calcium oxalate stones; mother hyperemesis; paternal grandmother DM2.
Never smoker, no alcohol (pregnant), teacher.

Vitals: afebrile, BP 125/78, HR 88.
Exam: uncomfortable, shifting on the stretcher. Right CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft, no peritoneal signs. No vaginal bleeding.

UA: microscopic hematuria, nitrite and LE negative, rare WBC; no sign of infection. Culture sent.
CBC, BMP unremarkable, Cr 0.6.
Renal US (no CT in pregnancy): 5 mm right UVJ stone, mild right hydronephrosis, left kidney normal. Bedside view: IUP with cardiac activity.

Treatment: acetaminophen 1 g PO, 1 L LR. Pain from 9/10 to 3/10.

Impression: right ureterolithiasis, 5 mm distal stone, uncomplicated, in a 10-week pregnancy.
Plan: home. Acetaminophen 500 mg, 2 tabs every 6 hours as needed. Oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325, 1 tab every 6 h if pain is not controlled, #8, no refills. Strain urine, save the stone. Push fluids. Outpatient urology referral placed. OB notified. Return for fever, uncontrolled pain or vomiting, or bleeding.

documents.title: ED record 4/12/2026
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ED note from 4/12 received: right 5 mm UVJ stone at ~10 weeks pregnant, sent home with acetaminophen and a few oxycodone tabs, urology referral from the ED. Scanned, routed to PCP. Pt not seen here since 9/2025.

documents.title: Checking in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Leah, we got your ER record from the weekend. How is the pain today? Let us know if you need help getting in with urology or if anything gets worse.

documents.title: RE: Checking in
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. Comes and goes, mostly a dull ache now. Urology called me already, I see them May 6.

documents.title: Stone
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good news, I think I passed it last night! Caught it in the strainer. No pain at all this morning. Should I still go to urology?

documents.title: RE: Stone
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news. Yes, keep the urology visit and bring the stone with you. They'll want a quick ultrasound to make sure the kidney has drained, and they can talk about prevention given your uncle's history.

reports.text: Comparison 4/12/2026. Right kidney 11.1 cm and left kidney 11.0 cm with normal cortical thickness and echogenicity. No hydronephrosis on either side. No renal or ureterovesical junction stones seen. Bilateral ureteral jets present. Bladder normal.
reports.conclusion: Normal kidneys. Interval resolution of right hydronephrosis; no stones.

documents.title: Urology Consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE UROLOGY GROUP
Consultation, 5/6/2026
Referred from: emergency department. Copy to PCP.

27 y/o currently about 13 weeks pregnant, seen in the ED 4/12 with a 5 mm right UVJ stone and mild hydronephrosis. Passed the stone 4/20 into a strainer and has been pain-free since. No fever, no urinary symptoms. First stone. Maternal uncle with recurrent calcium oxalate stones.
Meds: prenatal vitamin. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: well, no CVA tenderness.
Renal ultrasound today: no hydronephrosis, no residual stones.

Assessment: right distal ureteral stone, passed spontaneously; obstruction resolved.
Plan:
- Fluids 2.5 to 3 liters a day, enough that urine stays pale.
- No routine imaging in pregnancy unless symptoms return.
- With a family history of recurrent stones, a metabolic evaluation (24-hour urine) is reasonable once she is done with pregnancy and nursing; she can call us then.
- Follow up as needed.

documents.title: Urology letter received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Urology consult 5/6/2026 received and scanned: stone passed, ultrasound clear, 24-hr urine after pregnancy. Routed to PCP for review.

Complete anatomy survey normal including brain, face, spine, heart with four chambers and outflow tracts, abdomen, kidneys, bladder and limbs. Anterior placenta, clear of the os. Normal amniotic fluid. Cervical length normal.
